failed.check: Couldn't check the agents on this PC.

agents.firstHint: This AI is used both when you talk in the input box and when tasks are worked on. You can change it later in the settings.
agents.found: Installed. Works with a sign-in or an API key
agents.how: Run this command in a terminal and follow the prompts to sign in.
agents.lead: alpacawork hands the work to the AI agents already on this PC, such as Claude Code and Codex. The ones you enable become the choices for who to ask.
agents.missing: The {{command}} command was not found. Install it to use this agent
agents.noneReady: Install an agent or sign in to one, then choose “Check again”.
agents.stillSignedOut: {{name}} is still not signed in. Sign in from a terminal, then check again.
agents.title: Agents for your tasks

changedElsewhere: Changed in another view. Showing the current setting.

consent.body: Usage data includes the version, OS, and feature usage counts. Conversations, task contents, file names, and the PC name are never sent. Nothing is sent until you go to the next step, and alpacawork works the same with this off. You can see what is sent and change this anytime in Settings.
consent.failed: Couldn't save your usage data choice. Try again.
consent.label: Send usage data to the developers

rows.id: A random ID for each PC (not derived from your PC or user information)
rows.notSent: Conversations, task titles and bodies, files and file names, the PC name, and user names
rows.sent: The alpacawork version, OS and device type, feature usage counts, screen load times, error types, the kinds of agents used, and approximate task counts
rows.stop: In Settings → General → Usage data, you can see what will be and was sent, stop sending, and delete the data already sent

display.lead: Choose the language and colors for the alpacawork screen.
display.title: Language and theme

done.appBody: Even after you close the tab, you can open alpacawork from its icon in the Dock or the taskbar.
done.later: You can also install it later in {{settings}} → {{apps}}.
done.menuBody: Install it with <ui>File</ui> → <ui>Add to Dock</ui> in the menu (macOS Sonoma or later), and you can open it again from its icon in the Dock.
done.title: Setup is done

project.cwdHint: Choose a repository you already have and the AI works there. To just try it out, you can leave this empty ({{path}} is used).
project.gone: The project created during setup no longer exists. Finish setup, then create a project from the project menu.
project.lead: A project is a folder where the AI works, together with the rules for working there (the project policy).
project.policyNote: Write the rules for this project here. You can leave it empty.
project.title: First project

alpacawork-betterquality.title: Checked by another AI before you see it
alpacawork-betterquality.what: Except for light work, before you are asked to review a result, an AI other than the one that built it checks it, and what it finds is fixed. This takes more time and tokens.

askmeclearly.title: Shorter, easier-to-read questions and reports
askmeclearly.what: When the AI asks you to decide something or reports a result, it shows where to look with images or video.

doyourjob.title: Fewer questions for you
doyourjob.what: The AI asks you only what you alone can decide, and finds out the rest itself.

skills.lead: Skills change how the AI works.

reason.link_conflict: Another item with the same name is already in the Claude Code skills folder (~/.claude/skills). It was left unchanged.
reason.npm: The installer failed. Check that npm works and that GitHub is reachable, then try again.
reason.other: Try again, or continue without it.
reason.timeout: The installation timed out. Try again.
reason.unreachable: Couldn't reach the download source. Check your network connection, then try again.

skills.title: Skills to install
skills.where: Installs to {{place}}. They also apply when you use Claude Code outside alpacawork.

title: Setup
